newsitem.title: USA: ABT VP says $0.55 Q1 EPS view too bullish.
newsitem.headline: ABT VP says $0.55 Q1 EPS view too bullish.

text.p: The vice president of finance for ABT Building Products Corp, Joseph O'Neill, said on Wednesday that some analysts had been too bullish in their first quarter estimates of $0.55 per share.
He said $0.52 per share was more realistic due to the recent mid-west floods which hampered the home building industry.
However, O'Neill said that due to "pent-up" demand for home building materials, he supported the 1997 full year earnings per share consensus forecast of $2.30.

O'Neill also backed analysts' consensus forecasts of $2.65 per share in 1998 if business conditions remained stable. He said the company was expecting housing starts next year to remain at 1.4 million and for the repair and rehabilitation segment to advance by six percent to eight percent.
"Based on what we see, we should be okay," in reaching $2.65, O'Neill said in an interview after he and the company's chief executive George Brophy spoke to the Atlanta Society of Financial Analysts.
